summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted due to concern for disseminated zoster, given his immunocompromised state from multiple myeloma. He had a known herpes zoster rash in the T5 dermatome and developed new skin lesions, prompting hospitalization for IV acyclovir therapy. During his 4-day stay, the rash remained stable without evidence of dissemination, and the new lesions were determined to be hemangiomas. He received IV acyclovir for four days, was transitioned to oral therapy, and started on gabapentin for post-herpetic neuralgia prevention. His multiple myeloma treatment continued without complications, and COPD symptoms were managed with inhaled bronchodilators. He remained stable, afebrile, and was discharged home on updated antiviral and pain regimens with close oncology follow-up.
